name: capnp-list-concat
instr:
Please add schema-free list concatenation to `capnp`. It should combine lists from separate messages without dropping fields that the caller's schema doesn't know about.

Expose `capnp::any_pointer::Builder::set_list_concat(&mut self, values: &[capnp::any_pointer::Reader<'_>]) -> capnp::Result<()>` and `capnp::message::Builder::set_root_list_concat(&mut self, values: &[capnp::any_pointer::Reader<'_>]) -> capnp::Result<()>` on the existing generic message builder. Each replaces its destination with a deep copy of the input elements, in input order. Null inputs contribute no elements or type information; with no non-null inputs, produce a non-null empty void list.

If no input is inline-composite, all non-null inputs must use the same wire element encoding. If any input is inline-composite, produce an inline-composite list whose data-word count and pointer-slot count are the independent maxima across the inputs' wire layouts. Compact data elements contribute one data word, compact pointer elements contribute one pointer slot, and void elements contribute neither. Zero-fill missing fields. Bit lists cannot participate in this promotion. Empty non-null lists still contribute their declared layout.

Also expose `capnp::any_pointer::Builder::splice_list(&mut self, start: u32, delete_count: u32, values: &[capnp::any_pointer::Reader<'_>]) -> capnp::Result<()>`. Replace the zero-based range with the input elements, using the same layout rules with the destination's declared layout par
